sources.scope: General blood-test education: test description and result interpretation sections; not individual diagnosis.

scope: General blood-test education only, with the report's applicable laboratory interval. No pediatric, pregnancy-specific, disease-management or assay-specific targets.
overview: ALT is an enzyme concentrated mainly in the liver.
high: Liver-cell injury, infection or some medicines can increase ALT; exercise can also affect results.
low: Unusually low ALT may be associated with vitamin B6 deficiency or chronic kidney disease.
caveats: ALT level alone does not measure the extent of liver damage. Consider other liver tests and patient context; no medication changes are recommended here.
